chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Four prayers that a man should pray at any time: A missed prayer, so whenever you remember it, fulfill it; and the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf; and the prayer of the eclipse; and the funeral prayer. These four you may pray at all times.
ai.seo_question: Which four prayers can be performed at any time of day according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that these four specific prayers are exempt from the general prohibitions of *karahat* (disliked times) and *haram* (forbidden times) like sunrise and sunset, allowing them to be performed at any hour. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for acts of immediate obligation or strong recommendation, such as making up a missed *fard* prayer, the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, *Salat al-Kusuf* (eclipse prayer), and *Salat al-Mayyit* (funeral prayer). This ruling underscores the priority of fulfilling communal or time-sensitive duties over the temporal restrictions of general voluntary prayers.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

Four Salāts, the man should pray these during every timing – A Salāt which is missed out, so whenever you remember it, fulfil it; and a Salāt of two Rak’at for the Tawaaf is an Obligation; and Salāt of the eclipse; and the Salāt upon the deceased. You can pray these during all of the timings’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

There are four kinds of Salah (prayer) which a man can perform anytime. Such are Salah (prayer) after remembering a forgotten one, two Rak‘at after obligatory Tawaf, because of eclipse and Salah (prayer) for a deceased. You can perform these kinds of Salah (prayer) at any hour.’”
